kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: thumbnailer
  namespace: k8s-pod-security
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: thumbnailer}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: thumbnailer}
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "touch /tmp/ready && exec sleep infinity"]
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command: ["test", "-f", "/tmp/ready"]
            periodSeconds: 2

content.text: The cluster confirms four violations: `allowPrivilegeEscalation`, `capabilities.drop`, `runAsNonRoot`, and `seccompProfile`. The busybox image has no non-root `USER`, so I'll also set an explicit `runAsUser`. I'll edit the Deployment now.

input.old_string:
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "touch /tmp/ready && exec sleep infinity"]
input.new_string:
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "touch /tmp/ready && exec sleep infinity"]
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

content.text:
The `thumbnailer` pod now starts and passes its readiness probe in `k8s-pod-security`, and the namespace still enforces `restricted`.

I changed only `worker.yaml`. The Deployment had no `securityContext`, so it failed four `restricted` checks. I added a pod-level `runAsNonRoot`, `runAsUser: 1000`, and `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`, and a container-level `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`. The explicit `runAsUser` is needed because the busybox image has no non-root `USER`.
